title: Lazur vs Siri on Mac in 2026: which voice assistant fits your daily work
metaTitle: Lazur vs Siri on Mac: screen help, price and privacy compared
description: Lazur vs Siri on Mac: Lazur points at things on your screen from $18 a month. Siri AI is in beta, with no price stated yet.
intro: Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac that lives in the notch. It sees your screen, points at things and answers out loud, in any app. Siri is Apple's built-in assistant, and its new version, Siri AI, is still in beta. This page compares the two on price, platforms, privacy and screen help, so you can pick the one that fits your daily work.
tldr: Lazur is a Mac app you install. Siri ships with macOS, and Siri AI is in beta on macOS 27.
Lazur points at things on your screen and guides you one click at a time. Apple's Siri pages describe onscreen awareness, not pointing.
Lazur Pro costs $18/month after a 3-day trial. Apple states no price for Siri AI, so check their pricing page.
Siri AI needs a Mac with an M1 chip or later. Lazur also runs on Intel Macs.
Pick Lazur for guidance inside any app. Pick Siri for a built-in assistant that spans Apple devices, if you accept a beta.

blocks.text: Lazur and Siri do different jobs

Lazur is a third-party app you install on your Mac. Siri ships with macOS and needs no install. That difference shapes most of this comparison. Lazur is built to guide you through a task, one step at a time. Siri is built to answer questions and run actions across Apple's apps and devices. Both can help with the same question, but they hand you the answer in different ways.

Here is a quick way to see the gap. Open an app you rarely use, such as Pages or Numbers, and ask each assistant how to do one specific task. Lazur draws a circle and a label around the spot, then waits while you click. Apple describes Siri using onscreen awareness to answer. That is a different style, and Apple's pages do not describe pointing at a control.
What Siri AI is in 2026

Apple introduced Siri AI on June 8, 2026. Apple calls it an entirely new version of Siri. The September 2026 release says it is rolling out in beta, in English, in iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27, watchOS 27 and visionOS 27. Apple's support page, published November 5, 2026, lists six languages: English, French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish.

Beta means the feature is still changing. MacRumors' hands-on review says Apple 'is still refining' Siri AI. Plan on things shifting. Check Apple's support page before you rely on a specific behavior.
Which Macs can run Siri AI

Apple's support page lists macOS 27 Golden Gate for MacBook Neo and for any Mac with an M1 chip or later. Intel Macs are not on that list. If your Mac has an Intel chip, Siri AI is not an option today. Lazur still runs there, because it supports Intel Macs as well as Apple silicon.

To find your chip, choose Apple menu > About This Mac. The chip name sits near the top of the window. Apple silicon Macs show an M-series chip name. Intel Macs show an Intel processor name. If you see Intel, test Lazur first and skip Siri AI for now.

Lazur needs macOS, on Apple silicon or Intel. Windows is planned but not available. Siri AI also reaches iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch and Apple Vision Pro, which Lazur does not cover. If your work spans several Apple devices, that reach counts in Siri's favor.
How each one handles what is on your screen

Lazur works on the screen in front of you. Hold ⌥ ⌘, which is Option plus Command, and ask about anything you see. Lazur answers out loud. Ask where something is, and it draws a circle and a label around that spot. Ask how to do something, and it guides you one click at a time. It waits for each click before it moves to the next step.

Siri AI has onscreen awareness. Apple lists it next to personal context and app actions. Apple's pages describe Siri answering and acting on what it sees. They do not describe a pointing feature, or a step-by-step guide that waits for your click. Treat that as a gap in Apple's documentation, not proof the feature is missing.
Lazur vs Siri on a real task in an app you rarely use

Say you need to build a chart in Numbers, and you have never built one. Open the file and hold ⌥ ⌘. Ask where the chart tool lives. Lazur circles the button and labels it. Click it, then ask what comes next. Lazur waits. You click again. After a few rounds, you know the path and can repeat it alone.

Siri AI can give you the answer in one reply. That helps when you need a fact or a quick action. It helps less when you want to learn the steps yourself. If you want the path, not only the result, Lazur fits that job better.

items: Where is the export option in this window? Lazur circles the control and labels it. Siri answers from onscreen context.
Walk me through making a table from this list. Lazur guides you one click at a time and waits for each click.
Set a 25 minute timer and remind me to stretch at noon. Lazur handles timers and Reminders by voice.

blocks.text: Pricing: what Lazur costs and why Siri's price is unclear

Lazur starts with a 3-day Pro trial. The trial starts when you first open the app, and it needs no credit card. After the trial, Pro costs $18/month, or $15/month billed annually. Pro includes 150 AI actions. Power costs $120/month, or $96/month billed annually, and includes 1,000 AI actions. Dictation is unlimited on both plans.

Siri's price is not stated. Apple's Siri page says expanded access to some features 'will be available for a fee in the future.' It gives no amount. Apple also says some server features, including Siri AI, have daily usage limits, and those limits vary. Apple has not published numbers. Check their pricing page on apple.com/siri before you plan a budget.

Two mistakes come up here. First, people read 'in the future' as a price. It is not one. Second, people assume Siri is free because it ships with the Mac. Apple's page does not say that either. Use the prices you can confirm, and treat the rest as unknown.
Annual billing lowers the monthly rate, but it asks for a longer commitment. Run the trial first. Use it for a full work week, not one afternoon, so you see how often you reach for the shortcut.
Privacy: what each one stores and sends

Lazur listens and looks at your screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers so they can answer you. Lazur says neither is stored, and that content is never used to train AI models. Memory of what you asked and did stays on your Mac.

Apple's privacy page says audio data is not stored by Apple unless you opt in. It also says Siri data is not associated with your Apple Account. Request history links to a random device identifier. That identifier rotates multiple times per hour and is not tied to your Apple Account or email address.

Apple also says search requests are stored and used to improve Search, Siri and related features. Siri may send audio, Siri setup, contacts and location to Apple to process a request. If you opted in to improvement, Apple may store the audio and text of what you say. To turn that off, go to Settings > Privacy & Security > Analytics & Improvements.
Apple's June 2026 release calls Siri 'the world's most private digital assistant.' That is Apple's own claim and marketing language. Read it next to the storage details above, not in place of them.

Apple says personal data in requests handled by Private Cloud Compute is not stored or made accessible to Apple or anyone else. Those are Apple's statements, not independent audits. Lazur's data path is simpler to describe: audio and screenshots go to AI providers to answer, and Lazur says they are not stored.
Where Siri is the better pick

Siri ships with macOS, so there is nothing to install and no trial to start. It also covers more of your devices. Siri AI runs on iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch and Apple Vision Pro, if they meet Apple's requirements. Apple describes personal context and a Siri app with cross-device sync. If your day lives across several Apple devices, Siri has the wider reach.

Reviews are mixed, and they are opinions. MacRumors' hands-on review calls the new Siri 'smarter, more capable.' The Verge's hosts, as TechBuzz reports it, found Siri AI 'good enough at most things' and saw little that felt 'bleeding edge.' Read those as early impressions from a beta, not a final verdict.

Pick Siri if you want an assistant that comes with the Mac and you can accept a beta. Siri also fits if you mostly need facts, weather, music and quick web answers. A 2025 YouGov survey, reported by 9to5Mac, found 59% of voice assistant users check the weather and 51% play music. That survey covered voice assistants in general, not Siri AI.
Where Lazur is the better pick

Lazur works in any app, not only in Apple's own software. It guides you through a task one click at a time. It also runs on Intel Macs, which Siri AI does not list. Those three points matter most if you use third-party apps every day.

Lazur does more than answer. It runs research in its own Chrome tabs through the Lazur for Chrome extension, then returns a summary and a report. It sets timers, adds Apple Reminders and Calendar events, takes notes, controls music and volume, and opens apps and links.

Dictation is part of the package too. Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. Lazur adds snippets, a personal dictionary and clipboard slots. Dictation is included, but it is not the headline. If dictation is your main need, read [Lazur vs Apple Dictation on Mac](/compare/lazur-vs-apple-dictation) first.
Edge cases: offline use and where requests go

Lazur sends audio and screenshots to AI providers to answer, so those answers depend on that path. Apple says that with Siri AI off or unavailable, requests are processed on your device whenever possible. That is a real difference if you work where signal is weak. Test both before you rely on either one there.

With Siri AI on, a request may be processed on your device or sent to Private Cloud Compute. Apple's page does not list which requests go to Private Cloud Compute. Read the privacy section before you decide, especially if you handle client files or private notes.
Mistakes people make when they compare these two

items: Assuming Siri AI works everywhere. Apple says it is not available for iOS, iPadOS or watchOS in the EU at first. Apple Account regions in mainland China will not work either. Check Apple's support page for your region.
Mixing up Lazur with an automation tool. Lazur does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps. It points, explains and waits. You do the clicks.
Planning around Siri's limits. Apple publishes no numbers for daily limits. Lazur Pro includes 150 AI actions. Read the pricing page to see what counts as one action.
Forgetting when the trial starts. The 3-day Pro trial starts when you first open the app, not when you pay.
Buying for the Mac you have, then waiting for Siri AI. Apple's list starts at Macs with an M1 chip.
Ignoring the age rule. Apple says Siri AI is not available to users under 13.

blocks.text: Daily limits and heavy use

Siri's daily limits vary by feature, request complexity, system demand and policy. You cannot plan around them with Apple's numbers, because Apple publishes none. Lazur gives a fixed count: 150 AI actions on Pro and 1,000 on Power. If you expect heavy use, compare the Power count against a typical week.

Track the tasks where you reach for voice. A week of notes tells you more than a spec sheet. Write down each request, whether a circle or a spoken answer helped, and how long the task took. Then compare that log with the limits and prices above.
How to decide and what to do next

Start with the question you ask most often. If it sounds like 'where is this in this app,' test Lazur first. If it sounds like 'what's the weather' or 'set a timer,' Siri handles that kind of request too, so you may not need a second app.

items: Check your Mac. Choose Apple menu > About This Mac and read the chip name.
If you run Apple silicon and can install macOS 27, read Apple's Siri AI support page and decide whether a beta suits you.
Download Lazur from the [download page](/download) and start the 3-day Pro trial.
Hold ⌥ ⌘ in an app you use every day, and ask where one control is. Note whether the circle saves you time.
After a week, compare the time you saved with the price on the [pricing page](/pricing).

faq.question: Is Lazur better than Siri on a Mac?
faq.answer: It depends on the job. Lazur is better when you want guidance inside any app. It draws a circle around a control and waits while you click. Siri is better when you want a built-in assistant that works across Apple devices, with no install and no trial. Pick by the task, not by the brand.

faq.question: Can Siri AI run on my Intel Mac?
faq.answer: Not according to Apple's support page. It lists macOS 27 on MacBook Neo and on Macs with an M1 chip or later. Intel Macs are not on that list. Lazur runs on Intel Macs and on Apple silicon Macs.

faq.question: How much does Siri cost?
faq.answer: Apple has not stated a price. Its Siri page says expanded access to some features will be available for a fee in the future, and it gives no amount. Check the pricing page on apple.com/siri before you budget. Lazur Pro costs $18/month, or $15/month billed annually.

faq.question: Does Lazur click buttons or edit files for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons, edit files, or operate other apps for you. It points at things, explains them, and guides you one click at a time. You do the clicks, and Lazur waits for each one.

faq.question: Is Siri more private than Lazur?
faq.answer: Apple says Siri data is not tied to your Apple Account and that audio is not stored unless you opt in. Apple also stores search requests. Lazur says audio and screenshots go to AI providers to answer and are not stored, and that content is never used to train AI models. Both make claims, so read the privacy sections and pick the one you trust more.

faq.question: Which languages does Siri AI support?
faq.answer: Apple's support page lists English, French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish as currently available. Siri AI is in beta and is not available to users under 13. Check the page again before you rely on a specific language.

faq.question: Does Lazur work on Windows?
faq.answer: Not yet. Windows is planned, not available. Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon Macs and on Intel Macs.

verdict: Pick Lazur if you want guidance inside any app, on an Apple silicon or Intel Mac, with a trial you can test this week. Pick Siri if you want an assistant that ships with macOS, you use other Apple devices, and you can live with a beta. Siri's price is still unstated, so check their pricing page before you budget.
